name: tui-craft
description: Design, mock, build and review terminal user interfaces against a cell grid rather than against source code, because a string template does not tell you how many cells it occupies and that gap is where terminal defects live. Two skills. `tui-design` compiles a declarative spec into a real cell frame so the compiler does the width arithmetic instead of a model counting characters in a code block, then gates the design: role ladder, state that survives losing colour, focus on two channels. `tui-craft` captures the running app through a pty into a typed frame and runs the arithmetic gates on it (border integrity, cell-width, overflow, truncation markers, glyph risk), then applies a pattern catalogue drawn from 48 shipped TUIs and a cited set of terminal constraints. One width function serves both, so a mock and the capture it is compared against never disagree for reasons that are not about the design.
